title: Closed pushforward detects absolute finite-stage pseudo-coherence
statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose that the degree-zero complex $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)[0]$ is pseudo-coherent on $P$ [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. For every integer $m$ and every $K\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-pc-derived-category], $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $Z$ if and only if $Ri_*K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $P$ [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Here $i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is the ordinary direct-image structure module. No quasi-coherence, boundedness or Noetherian hypothesis on $K$, $Z$ or $P$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, restricted from ringed spaces to schemes.

proof.text: Write $B=i_*\mathcal O_Z$. The underlying abelian-sheaf functor $i_*$ is exact by [lem-sc-closed-immersion-pushforward-exact]. Kernels of module maps are sectionwise kernels and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; these are the same underlying abelian sheaves with the induced scalar action. Thus exactness also holds for $i_*:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Z)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_P)$. Applying it to kernels, images and their quotients gives $H^q(i_*E^\bullet)=i_*H^q(E^\bullet)$, naturally. The closed-pushforward stalk formula [lem-sc-closed-pushforward-abelian-stalks] shows that $i_*F=0$ implies $F=0$, and that the pushforward vanishes on $P\setminus i(Z)$. Indeed, if all germs of a section are zero, it vanishes on a neighbourhood of every point and hence vanishes by the sheaf axiom.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, opening paragraph: exactness and closed-support stalks

proof.text: Let $\mathcal E^\bullet$ be any complex representing $E\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$. By [def-pc-derived-direct-image] and [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], $Ri_*E$ is represented by $i_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ for any K-injective resolution $\mathcal E^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$, where the module direct image is $W\mapsto\mathcal F(i^{-1}W)$ with $\mathcal O_P$ acting through $i^\sharp$. This module functor is exact by Step 1, so by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] termwise $i_*$ carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Hence $i_*\mathcal E^\bullet\to i_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $Ri_*E\cong Q(i_*\mathcal E^\bullet)\cong F_D(E)$, naturally, with $F_D$ the triangulated functor of that node. Thus $Ri_*E$ is represented by termwise $i_*\mathcal E^\bullet$ for any representative, without boundedness; it commutes with shifts, and a distinguished triangle $A\to E\to C\to A[1]$ goes to the distinguished triangle $F_D(A)\to F_D(E)\to F_D(C)\to F_D(A)[1]$, whose terms are the termwise pushforwards. For an open $U\subset P$, with $V=i^{-1}U$ and $i_U:V\hookrightarrow U$, the equality $(i_*F)|_U=(i_U)_*(F|_V)$ follows on an open $W\subset U$ from both sides being $F(i^{-1}W)$. It holds termwise for complexes as well. We can therefore shrink the ambient open throughout the proof.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, opening paragraph and the repeated shrinking of X

proof.text: We use [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex] on schemes and the identical approximation condition on the site of open subsets of a scheme. Slice restriction there is ordinary restriction to the corresponding open, so the cited ringed-site lemmas apply to this condition. It is local by combining open covers. An $m$-approximation is also a $p$-approximation for $p\ge m$: at $p>m$ its cohomology map is already invertible. Such an approximation gives a local upper cohomology bound, namely the maximum of $m$ and the largest nonzero degree of its bounded strictly perfect source. If $H^q(E)=0$ for all $q\ge m$, the zero complex and its map to $E$ already give an $m$-approximation.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, both induction paragraphs: locality, boundedness and the case p<m

proof.text: For every integer $p$ and finite $r\ge0$, put $A=\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}[-p]$. It is $a$-pseudo-coherent for every $a$, using its identity as a strictly perfect approximation [def-pc-perfect-complex, def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Its termwise pushforward is $B^{\oplus r}[-p]$. By the hypothesis and [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], locally choose a bounded-above finite-free model $F^\bullet$ of $B[0]$. Then $(F^\bullet)^{\oplus r}[-p]$ models $B^{\oplus r}[-p]$. Its brutal truncation in degrees $\ge a$ maps to the model, is bounded finite free, and induces isomorphisms above $a$ and a surjection at $a$. Thus $i_*A$ is $a$-pseudo-coherent for every $a$ as well, including $a=m$ and $m+1$.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, both displayed triangles: pseudo-coherence of the shifted finite sums of the structure module

proof.text: Fix $m$. For each integer $p\ge m-1$ prove, by induction on the nonnegative integer $p-m+1$, both implications for every complex $E$ with $H^q(E)=0$ for $q>p$, locally at every point and for every ambient open restriction of $i$. For $p=m-1$ both $E$ and $i_*E$ have no cohomology in degrees $\ge m$ by Step 1, so Step 3 proves both assertions. For the induction step $p\ge m$, assume both implications at $p-1$ for every such local restriction. It suffices to work at $z\in Z$; points of $P\setminus i(Z)$ have zero pushforward. The next steps construct, after shrinking around $z$, a cone with upper bound $p-1$.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, both paragraphs: explicit induction on an upper bound, rather than assuming a largest nonzero degree exists

proof.text: Suppose first that $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. By Step 3 it is $p$-pseudo-coherent. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-site-pseudocoherent-top-finite-type] on the open-subset site of $Z$, with its integer parameter equal to $p$, to obtain that $H^p(E)$ is locally of finite type. Suppose instead that $i_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. The same argument on $P$ gives finite type of $H^p(i_*E)=i_*H^p(E)$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], choose finitely many generating sections on an ambient neighbourhood $U$ of $i(z)$. They are sections of $H^p(E)$ on $V=i^{-1}U$. At every $w\in V$ their germs generate $H^p(E)_w$ already with scalars from $\mathcal O_{P,i(w)}$, by [lem-sc-closed-pushforward-abelian-stalks]. Consequently they also generate with scalars from $\mathcal O_{Z,w}$. Thus in either case, locally around $z$, we have finitely many sections generating $H^p(E)$. To check local generation from these germs, express the germ of any section as a finite linear combination, represent its coefficients near the point and shrink once more to make the equality hold. This gives local surjectivity and hence an epimorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] on the open-subset site.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, forward finite-cohomology sentence and reverse finite-cohomology/adjunction paragraph

proof.text: Choose any complex $E^\bullet$ representing $E$. The quotient map $\ker(d^p:E^p\to E^{p+1})\to H^p(E^\bullet)$ is an epimorphism of underlying abelian sheaves: its cokernel is zero by the cokernel description in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] on the open-subset site to each of the finitely many generating sections from Step 6. Choose a common neighbourhood of $z$ on which all lift, by intersecting the finitely many neighbourhoods containing $z$. Their lifts $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in\ker d^p$ define the chain map $\alpha:\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus r}[-p]\to E^\bullet$, $e_j\mapsto t_j$; it is a chain map precisely because $d^pt_j=0$. Its map on $H^p$ is surjective. Each open neighbourhood of $z$ in $Z$ is $i^{-1}U'$ for an ambient open $U'$, so this shrinking is allowed in the induction. Rank zero needs no lifts.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, the two constructions of a map from a finite free module in degree p

proof.text: Complete $\alpha:A\to E$ to a distinguished triangle $A\to E\to C\to A[1]$ using (TR1) of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. By [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], $H^q(C)=0$ for $q>p$ since $H^q(E)=0$ there and $H^{q+1}(A)=0$; also $H^p(C)=0$ since $H^p(A)\to H^p(E)$ is surjective and $H^{p+1}(A)=0$. Thus $C$ has upper bound $p-1$. Step 2 sends this to the distinguished triangle $i_*A\to i_*E\to i_*C\to(i_*A)[1]$. The objects $A$ and $i_*A$ are both $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent and $m$-pseudo-coherent by Step 4.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, the two pairs of displayed triangles and the cohomology bound of their cone

proof.text: For the forward implication, apply clause (1) of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-m-pseudocoherent-triangle] to $A\to E\to C$: $A$ is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent and $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, hence $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. The induction hypothesis at $p-1$ gives $i_*C$ $m$-pseudo-coherent after further shrinking. Clause (2) of that same node applied to $i_*A\to i_*E\to i_*C$, with both outer objects $m$-pseudo-coherent, gives that $i_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, end of the forward induction

proof.text: For the reverse implication, start with $i_*E$ $m$-pseudo-coherent. Clause (1) of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-m-pseudocoherent-triangle], applied to the pushed-forward triangle and the $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent object $i_*A$, gives $i_*C$ $m$-pseudo-coherent. The reverse induction hypothesis at $p-1$ gives $C$ $m$-pseudo-coherent. Clause (2) applied to $A\to E\to C$ then gives $E$ $m$-pseudo-coherent. This completes the simultaneous induction. Finally, when either side of the original equivalence is $m$-pseudo-coherent, Step 3 supplies a local upper bound on that side and Step 1 transfers it to the other. Apply the induction locally and combine the neighbourhoods by locality. Thus no global upper bound, quasi-coherence or Noetherian hypothesis was introduced.

source.place: Tag 09VA, lemma-closed-push-pseudo-coherent, end of the reverse induction and globalization
